whatIs: simpleParallax.js is a library that adds a parallax effect to the images on a page: as you scroll, the image moves and scales within its container. There's a plain JavaScript version and a React one, with next/image support in Next.js, and you install it with npm install simple-parallax-js.
It's a good fit when you want a simple parallax on images in a few lines, without setting up a full animation library.
uses: Adding depth to the images of a hero or a gallery as you scroll.
Wrapping a next/image image with SimpleParallax on a site built with Next.js.
Adjusting orientation, scale (1.4 by default), or delay to vary the effect between sections.
caveats: It applies to img tags (and video too), not to background images defined in CSS.
The scale must be greater than 1.0, and the higher it is, the more quality the image loses: use a proportionally larger image, for example 750 px wide to display it at 500 px with a scale of 1.5.
If you enable overflow, the image spills out of its container as it moves and can cover nearby content.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license.
idealFor: Sites with large images that want parallax without the hassle.
